content.text:
`python3 -m unittest -q` now passes, all 7 tests. That took two code fixes and one change to a test, which you should check.

**Code fixes in `household/bills.py`:**
1. **`split_bill`** dropped the leftover cents, so the shares added up to less than the bill (1001 split two ways gave `[500, 500]`). Now the leftover cents go one each to the first people, as the docstring says: `[501, 500]`.
2. **`due_dates`** crashed when the payments ran past December, because it tried to build "month 13". It now moves into the next year correctly (Nov 2026 → Dec 2026 → Jan 2027).

**Test change in `tests/test_bills.py`:**
- `test_three_ways` expected `split_bill(1000, 3) == [333, 333, 333]`. That adds up to 999 cents, not 1000. It contradicts the docstring and `test_remainder_goes_to_the_first`, so no version of the code could pass all of them. I changed the expected result to `[334, 333, 333]`. If you actually want leftover cents dropped, tell me and I'll change the docstring and the remainder test instead.

Nothing is committed.
